title: Chondriosomes and similar fibrils are surface-tension clumps drawn along the cell axis

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Chondriosomes and similar fibrils are surface-tension clumps drawn along the cell axis

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The mitochondria, chondriosomes and similar granules and fibrils of cells are not special entities with specific functions but clumps of heterogeneous cell contents gathered by surface tension and drawn out along the cell axis by osmotic currents arising from surface energy and adsorption, revealing a field of force and dynamical polarity in the cell.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VI: A Note on Adsorption

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: while, from the physical point of view we are tempted to see but little mystery in the whole phenomenon, and to ascribe it, in all probability and in general terms, to the gathering or “clumping” together, under surface tension, of various constituents of the heterogeneous cell-content, and to the drawing out of these little clumps along the axis of the cell towards one or other of its extremities

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VI, “A Note on Adsorption”; topic “Polarity and chondriosomes”. Scope: fibrillar and granular cytoplasmic structures of epithelial, gland, nerve and germ cells

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch06-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern molecular and imaging databases can strongly discriminate special organelles from nonspecific clumps for many cell types. The full generalization and proposed physical transport mechanism remain only partly testable from existing archived data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test whether mitochondrial and fibrillar structures have stable molecular identities and functions and whether their axial distributions are better predicted by active transport and organelle biogenesis than by passive surface-tension clumping.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The claim combines several distinct structures and cell types.

Surface tension and osmotic currents are not directly measured in most archives.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim denies that mitochondria and similar granules are special entities and treats them as surface-tension clumps. Open proteomes and image volumes show membrane-bounded organelles with pathway annotations and a cell-wide distribution, which is a direct and standard test of that denial. A counterexample of this clarity resolves the universal claim even though some minor fibrillar inclusions remain less studied.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Ask whether mitochondria are bounded organelles with a characteristic proteome and functions, or unstructured clumps of mixed cytoplasm drawn to a cell pole. A double membrane, a mitochondrial proteome and a distributed network would refute the clump account; granules with no specific composition, gathered and drawn out with the cell axis, would support it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Mammalian cultured cells dominate the image sets relative to germ cells and invertebrate tissues.

The same resources do not cover every non-mitochondrial fibril the wording also includes.

operationalizability: 0.8
